newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices flat, deals loom.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices flat, deals loom.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds opened flat in typically sluggish Monday trade as players eyed the week's estimated $4.8 billion new issue calendar, expected to be the year's biggest so far.
"The market's in good shape. There aren't a lot of bonds around, there's a lot of money around," a municipal trader said. "The other side of the coin is we have a pretty good calendar."
A second trader said while Monday's muni cash market was largely unchanged, "everything gapped up pretty good Friday."

"The only stuff I saw really trade or have a huge follow through was index-related bonds," the trader said. "I think there were a lot of guys short the contract, and I think they were getting squeezed pretty hard Friday. Nobody expected this run up."

Munis ended Friday's session up 3/4 of a point, lagging U.S Treasury bonds' 1-1/4 point gain. Treasuries' improved when, after a mixed May employment report, talk surfaced of a delay in the European Economic and Monetary Union that was said to spur foreign buying of U.S. assets.
Monday's actively quoted municipal issues included Cleveland Ohio, Stadium Project 5-1/4 certificates of participation of November 2022. The bonds had a 5.58 percent net bid, unchanged from Friday.
In the government market, Monday saw the benchmark 30-year bond down 8/32 at 97-25/32 to yield 6.80 percent amid profit taking.
In debt futures, the September muni contract was down 5/32 at 117-4/32. The September T-bond contract was down 8/32 at 110-31/32. The MOB spread was 197 ticks.
As for the week's calendar, 63 negotiated offerings are expected to total $2.7 billion. A $540 million Puerto Rico Public Building Authority deal through Smith Barney Inc. tops the list.
On the competitive side, 89 sales totaling $2 billion are scheduled. A $225 million Virginia Housing Development Authority issue on Tuesday is expected to be the largest.
An additional 13 sales totaling $488 million are on the possible calender, meaning underwriters have said they may price the issues this week depending on market conditions.
